title: Read a travel note without guessing
summary: A note names a pier and a day. Find the two facts it gives and spot the one it leaves out.
requires: Sign in to AI Studio in a browser. Use a practice chat.
features: Send a note through Playground and match the answer against the note.
roles: Find a mail notice with a missing time.
Read a date from a team notice.
Show which trip details still need filling in.
prompt: Read just this note: Harbor shuttle boards at Pier 4 on March 8. Bring the blue ticket. Return three lines called Pier, Date and Time. Write unknown if the note leaves a fact out. Use the date exactly as given.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat.
steps.help: The Playground has a message box and a Run button. The Build view shows an app preview instead.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Find each answer in the note with your finger. Read the date carefully.
steps.help: The three answers are Pier 4, March 8 and unknown. No year appears.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: In a new chat, add Boarding begins at 09:15 to the note. Keep the same question and run again.
steps.help: If a time or year appears in the first answer, ask the helper to show the exact words that prove it.

check: The three answers are Pier 4, March 8 and unknown. No year appears.
Only Time changes. It now says 09:15. The date still has no year.
sources: Google AI Studio · Playground and run settings

title: Keep the same rule for three turns
summary: An unassigned ferry ticket names a topic but leaves its owner empty. Write one standing rule for a stack of topic cards. Each answer should use only its own card.
requires: Sign in to AI Studio in a browser. Use a practice chat.
features: Use System Instructions, a rule box that stays in place for a chat.
roles: Keep each mail request paired with its owner.
Read meeting cards one at a time.
Give each quiz card its own topic.
prompt: Card H2. Topic: Ferries. No owner is assigned. Give me the two fields my standing rule asks for.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. Open System instructions. Put the short rule in that box.
steps.help: A system instruction is a rule for each turn in this chat. The separate chat box is for a single card or question.
steps.code: Return only Topic | Owner. Copy the stated topic and owner exactly. Use UNASSIGNED when the card has no named owner.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Read the first reply. In the same chat send Card K4. Topic: Trains. Owner: Team One. Keep each answer on its own row.
steps.help: The first row is Ferries | UNASSIGNED. The second is Trains | Team One.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Send Card R9. Topic: Maps. Look at its owner box before reading earlier rows.
steps.help: If Maps gets Team One, add that each card starts with empty fields. Run all three cards again in order.

check: The first row is Ferries | UNASSIGNED. The second is Trains | Team One.
The last row is Maps | UNASSIGNED. Team One belongs only to Trains.
sources: Google AI Studio · Playground and run settings

title: Sort four help slips into trays
summary: Teach the helper when to choose one tray, two trays or the tray marked unknown.
requires: Sign in to AI Studio in a browser. Use a practice chat.
features: Give Playground labeled examples, then test it with fresh slips.
roles: Sort mail help slips.
Send file questions to the right team.
Sort feedback for a small app.
prompt: Use MAIL for a bounced letter and FILES for a document that will not open. Use BOTH when both things happen. Use UNKNOWN for just please help. Label four slips in order: A mail came back, B document does not load, C please help, D mail returned and document fails. Give just the ID and tray for each. Give UNKNOWN to every slip that mentions neither mail nor files.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat.
steps.help: The Playground has a message box and a Run button. The Build view shows an app preview instead.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Cover the reply with your hand. Predict the four trays yourself, then compare them one by one.
steps.help: A is MAIL, B is FILES, C is UNKNOWN and D is BOTH.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Replace slip A with the cafeteria is closed. Start a fresh chat with the same examples. Try the whole set again.
steps.help: If D gets just one tray, add a new teaching example with two problems and the label BOTH. Test with the original slips again.

check: A is MAIL, B is FILES, C is UNKNOWN and D is BOTH.
Only A changes. It now goes in UNKNOWN.
sources: Google AI Studio · Playground and run settings

title: Match a claim to the right notice
summary: A draft and an approved notice give different days. Find the date a reader can actually use.
requires: Sign in to AI Studio in a browser. Use a practice chat.
features: Ask Playground to quote a named source for an answer.
roles: Find the mail notice that supports a deadline.
Check a date against the approved plan.
Show a source under an app's answer.
prompt: Read just these three slips. M1 says Draft: Pier 2 opens June 3. M2 says Approved: Pier 2 opens June 8. M3 says Approved: Pier 4 opens June 9. When is Pier 2 approved to open? When does it close? Give the slip ID and its words for each answer, or say no source gives it.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. Leave web search off for this test.
steps.help: The Playground has a message box and a Run button. The Build view shows an app preview instead.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Look at the pier number and the word Approved on each slip. Match both clues before accepting a date.
steps.help: M2 supports June 8. None of the slips gives a closing date.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Remove M2 and ask again in a fresh chat. Check whether an approved date for Pier 2 still exists.
steps.help: If June 9 appears, ask the helper to quote its pier number. If June 3 appears, ask whether its slip was approved.

check: M2 supports June 8. None of the slips gives a closing date.
The approved opening date for Pier 2 is now unknown.
sources: Google AI Studio · Playground and run settings

title: Give an app a clean date box
summary: Three launch notices describe dates with different levels of certainty. Turn three launch cards into records an app can read. Leave a missing date empty on purpose.
requires: Sign in to AI Studio in a browser. Use a practice chat.
features: Use structured output, a set of named boxes a program can read.
roles: Read dates from sample mail notices.
Bring form dates into a staff list.
Save planned launch dates in an app.
prompt: Read three cards. C1 says Launch 2027-04-02. C2 says Date to be announced. C3 says Tentative 2027-05-09. Return the ID and stated date for each in order. Keep the tentative date. Write null when there is no date. Null is the computer's empty marker.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. In Run settings turn on structured output. Paste the shape, or use the editor to add the same fields.
steps.help: Choose a model that offers structured output. The two field names are id and date.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Compare each record with its card. Look closely at the middle date field. It should hold the empty marker, without quotes.
steps.help: The dates are 2027-04-02, null and 2027-05-09, in order.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Use the same shape in a fresh run. Change only C3 to 2027-05-10. Compare all three records.
steps.help: If C2 contains a made-up date, ask for an empty date when the card gives none. Check the field in the actual result.

check: The dates are 2027-04-02, null and 2027-05-09, in order.
Only C3 changes to May 10. C2 stays empty.
sources: Google AI Studio · Playground and run settings

writeYourOwn.goal: Turn three launch notes into dated app records.
writeYourOwn.given: C1 gives April 2, 2027. C2 has no date. C3 tentatively says May 9, 2027.

roles: Count zero-error checks in a mail report.
Check a total in a shared table.
Add positive and negative game scores.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. In Run settings choose a model with Code execution and turn it on.
steps.help: Open the code and its result after the run. If the switch is missing, choose a model that offers it.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Open the code and its printed result. Add each team's points on paper before comparing.
steps.help: Red has 12 in two rounds. Blue has 5 in two rounds. The grand total is 17.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Replace Blue,8 with Blue,-8 and run again. Count the played rounds a second time.
steps.help: If Red has one round, mark a zero as played. If Red has three, make sure the word blank is skipped.

check: Red has 12 in two rounds. Blue has 5 in two rounds. The grand total is 17.
Blue now has -11. The grand total is 1. Each team still has two played rounds.

title: Judge two models with the same scorecard

features: Try two model choices and grade them with one answer key.
roles: Check two explanations of a mail rule.
Compare helpers on one staff task.
Pick a helper for a game's rules page.
prompt: A pretend lot charges 2 dollars per started hour up to 8 dollars. Entries at or after 18:00 cost 3 dollars flat. All visits end the same day. A stays 17:30–19:45, B stays 18:00–18:20 and C stays 09:00–15:00. Give each fee and say which clock time picks the rule.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat.
steps.help: The Playground has a message box and a Run button. The Build view shows an app preview instead.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Run it in two fresh chats with different models or thinking levels. Give one point per correct fee and one for using the entry time. Record scores out of four.
steps.help: A costs 6 dollars, B costs 3 and C costs 8. Entry time picks the rule.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Move A's entry to 18:01. Keep the same exit. Try the change with both models and record how long each takes.
steps.help: If a helper charges A the evening price in the first round, ask which time on the ticket it used.

check: A costs 6 dollars, B costs 3 and C costs 8. Entry time picks the rule.
A now costs 3 dollars. The other fees stay the same. A tie is a possible result.

title: Ask the catalog before naming a shelf

Find the owner of a sample team file.
Ask a game library where a title belongs.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. Turn on Function calling in Run settings. Add the tool description. For two tools, use one description per tool if the editor asks.

steps.help: First comes a request for BK17. Only after the tool reply does the answer give H-04.

steps.title: Try a second case

steps.help: If your screen cannot enter a tool reply, write the request and reply as two lines on paper. A practice dialogue is not proof a real tool ran.

check: First comes a request for BK17. Only after the tool reply does the answer give H-04.
The shelf is unknown. No invented shelf number appears.

title: Test what the model can actually see

features: Attach a picture, then compare the reply with a run that has no picture.
roles: Read the labels on a pretend report picture.
Compare a slide with its written description.

steps.title: Try a second case

The reply asks for an image or says it cannot see the panels.

Fix missing dates on a practice list.
Make a working data-entry page.

steps.help: If you see only a text answer, return to Build and open the preview.

steps.text: Set N2 to 2027-06-04. Export and count the records. Clear N1 and try to export again.

title: Find the rule that applied that day
summary: A rule can be approved today and start later. Work out which rule was in force on each day.
requires: Sign in to AI Studio in a browser. Use a practice chat.
features: Put the date rules in System Instructions and the sample slips in the message box.
roles: Find the mail rule in effect on a sample date.
Read an approved team policy by date.
Apply a game's rules for the right season.
prompt: Use these made-up records for 2027. P1 is approved and starts July 1 with cap 4. P2 is a draft for July 8 with cap 9. P3 is approved and starts July 12 with cap 6. Give the cap on June 30, July 10 and July 12. Include the ID of the rule you used.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. Open System instructions. Put the short rule in that box. Leave web search off for this test.
steps.help: A system instruction is a rule for each turn in this chat. The separate chat box is for a single card or question.
steps.code: Consider only approved records effective on or before the query date. Use the latest effective date. If two eligible records tie on that date and disagree, return CONFLICT with both IDs. With no eligible record, return UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Check approval first. Cross off any rule that starts after the day in the question. Pick the latest one still on the list.
steps.help: The answers are UNKNOWN, 4 from P1, and 6 from P3.

steps.title: Try a second case
steps.text: Add P4, approved for July 12 with cap 5. Run the same three days again using the rule in System instructions.
steps.help: If 9 appears, check P2's draft label. If one July 12 rule wins after P4 arrives, check for a tie on the start date.

check: The answers are UNKNOWN, 4 from P1, and 6 from P3.
July 12 is CONFLICT with P3 and P4. Neither earlier answer changes.
sources: Google AI Studio · Playground and run settings

title: Pass one tool's answer to the next
summary: Find a boat's ID, then use that ID to look up its next stop. Try both a match and a missing boat.

features: Watch the ID from one pretend lookup become the input for the next lookup.
roles: Use a test mail ID to find its report.
Use a file ID to find a sample owner.
Use a game ID to look up its rules.

title: Score a prompt on new examples
summary: Try two ways to explain a color rule. Check whether the better explanation also works on numbers it has never seen.

roles: Test a mail warning color rule.
Check a report's status labels.
Test a game's difficulty labels.
prompt: Use RED for a whole number of 10 or more, AMBER for 5 to 9 and GREEN for 0 to 4. Use UNKNOWN for missing, negative or non-whole numbers. Give just ID and label. Try A=0, B=4, C=5, D=9, E=10, F=missing, G=-1, H=4.5.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat.
steps.help: The Playground has a message box and a Run button. The Build view shows an app preview instead.

steps.title: Run the prompt
steps.text: Paste the lab prompt. Select Run. Score one point per right label. In a new chat with the same model add this rule: First check that the number exists and is whole and at least zero. Score it again.
steps.help: A through H should give GREEN, GREEN, AMBER, AMBER, RED, UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Try a second case

title: Price each useful answer
summary: Two models charge different prices and pass different numbers of the same cases. Count what the practice helpers cost, including tries you pay for twice. All prices here are made up for a math game.

features: Use Code execution to add the cost of each paid practice try.
roles: Price a practice mail help task.
Compare two sample document-review plans.
Budget the cost of a game's hint button.

Test Quick alone, Deep alone, and Quick on all followed by Deep on E,F,G,H. On those four keep Deep's answer. Report total cents, correct answers and cents per correct answer.

steps.title: Open a fresh chat
steps.text: Open Google AI Studio in a browser. Go to Playground. Start a new chat. In Run settings choose a model with Code execution and turn it on.
steps.help: Open the code and its result after the run. If the switch is missing, choose a model that offers it.

steps.title: Set up the practice space
steps.text: Sign in to Google AI Studio in a computer browser. Open Build and choose a new app.
